The guard checks if `agent.ownerId` matches `member.id`. For scope, I'm keeping ghost message attachments in memory only—never persisting them to disk—so they're served over HTTP but cleared when the window closes. I'm also making `statusOf` skip ghost runs entirely.

Beyond that, a ghost thread only routes to agents you own, so the prompt stays on your machine and doesn't leak to other users' CLIs. On the UI, I'll surface that constraint so users know why a ghost command might fail if they try to target someone else's agent. And I need a test that boots a real host, sends `/ghost` with an image, then walks the entire `.crew` directory to verify nothing was written to disk—no files, no text, no bytes.

The tradeoff: in a multi-person session, if you try `@Fable /ghost` where Fable belongs to Ali, you'll get a private message saying that agent runs elsewhere. Solo sessions are unaffected since all agents are yours. And `soloAgent()` with a single agent handles the edge case where you've joined someone's crew but have no agent of your own—the ghost gets refused, which is correct.

Now for the persistence layer: ghost events skip the log entirely, so threads reconstructed from events never see them. The in-memory queue stays in-memory, `chatLog` only appends via `appendEvent`, and the `this.events` array excludes ghost events since emit returns early.
